title: stream resume token + schema-compat mapping for safer tool calls and OpenAI compat
author: Marco Chen
description: Motivation: Partial/invalid structured outputs during streaming combined with in-flight tool/function-calls cause two classes of customer-visible issues: 1) callers get malformed JSON mid-stream and cannot recover, and 2) tool/instrumentation layers receive partial function calls or ambiguous tool arguments. This PR introduces a stream-resume token and a schema-compatibility mapper that together allow the runtime and OpenAI-compat layer to either recover the stream or fail fast with deterministic error codes. Changes: add a Resume-Token mechanism attached to streaming frames, implement a schema-compat mapper that translates legacy "openai-style" response_format hints into the new json-schema-v3 validation rules, fence tool/function-call events to commit only after a schema checkpoint is reached, and surface structured error codes with guidance for client retry. Design summary: 1) Streaming frames now optionally include "resume_token" when the runtime writes a schema checkpoint. Clients resuming a stream can present the token to start decoding from a later KV cache state. 2) Schema-compat mapper uses a small rule table to coerce/alias field names and types for backward compatibility (configurable per-customer via response_format flags). 3) Toolcall fencing defers tool invocation events until an explicit schema-commit frame is emitted; if a schema violation is detected prior to commit we emit an error frame with an idempotent error code and cancellation signal. 4) OpenAI-compat layer maps older error strings into the new structured error model so downstream SDKs receive stable error types. Implementation notes: runtime changes in serving/runtime/streaming.go handle token generation and KV checkpointing; api/gateway/response_format.go contains the compatibility mapper and per-tenant toggles; sdk-shims in openai_compat/translate handle error mapping for older clients. Tests: extended streaming integration tests to exercise resume on truncated streams, added toolcall fencing unit tests, compatibility matrix tests for three legacy response_format permutations. Migration: default behavior is backward-compatible (resume token emitted only when response_format=json_schema_v3 or tenant opt-in). A feature flag "stream_resume.enabled" governs rollout. Rollout plan: enable for internal canaries for 48h, measure stream recover rate and tail latency, then staged rollout to 10%, 50%, 100% of tenants. Observability: new metrics stream.resume_emitted, stream.resume_used, stream.fenced_toolcall_count and schema.compat_coercions. Security/Privacy: resume tokens are short-lived and HMAC-signed with tenant key; no additional user data is persisted beyond existing KV caches. "Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] compatibility tests, [x] docs update in redwood-docs/streams, [x] canary rollout plan included."
commits_summary: 3 commits: initial runtime and proto changes; compatibility mapper and sdk shim; tests and docs. Each commit focused: (1) stream resume token and KV checkpoint plumbing; (2) schema-compat and toolcall fencing logic + error mapping; (3) tests, docs, and rollout flags.
review_comments: Aisha Patel: Why are resume tokens tied to json_schema_v3 by default? We should avoid surprising customers who use earlier formats.

Marco Chen: Good point. Default behavior remains unchanged for legacy formats; resume token is emitted only when tenant opts in or response_format=json_schema_v3. Added explicit note in docs and feature flag gating.
Leah Ortega: Please add a unit test that validates HMAC rejection on tampered resume tokens.
Marco Chen: Added hmac tamper test and a negative integration test in tests/integration/stream_resume_test.go#tamper_case.
Samir Gupta: Benchmarks show tail latency +8% in synthetic p95 for small sequences. Can we micro-opt the checkpoint path?
Marco Chen: We moved token generation off the hot path and reuse a preallocated buffer; p95 dropped to +2% in the latest bench run. Kept the benchmark doc entry to show numbers and mitigations.
release_notes: Add streaming resume tokens and schema-compat mapping to reduce failures on partial structured output during streaming. Tool/function calls are now fenced until schema checkpoints, reducing spurious tool invocations. Feature gated behind stream_resume.enabled and opt-in response_format=json_schema_v3 for backward compatibility. Metrics and rollout plan included.
notes_for_backport: No backport required for release/* unless teams opt-in; if backporting, ensure featureflag yaml and HMAC key rotation migration are included.
qa_notes: Manual test steps included in docs: (1) start a stream with response_format=json_schema_v3 and capture resume_token; (2) simulate truncated connection and resume using token; (3) verify tool calls are not invoked until schema commit frame; (4) validate error mapping for legacy clients by toggling openai_compat in gateway config.
additional_context: Related to ENG-4721 (streaming stability) and SUP-3321 (customer reported tool call duplication). This PR unblocks a follow-up that will add client-side automatic resume in SDKs.
